title: Should You Hire a Lawyer After a St. Louis Crash?
metaDescription: Should you hire a lawyer after a St. Louis accident? Missouri fault rules, injury severity, and free matching options.
excerpt: Educational St. Louis, MO guide — 5-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: Signs you may need counsel
paragraphs: Hospitalization, surgery, disputed fault, denied coverage, or lowball offers after St. Louis crashes are common triggers for attorney consultation.

sections.heading: How Missouri contingency fees typically work
paragraphs: Most personal injury attorneys work on contingency — you pay no upfront fee; they receive a percentage of recovery if successful. Verify terms in writing.

sections.heading: What an attorney handles
paragraphs: Evidence preservation, lien negotiation, insurer correspondence, and litigation if settlement fails.

sections.heading: WreckMatch's role
paragraphs: We match St. Louis residents with independent Missouri attorneys. We are not a law firm and do not provide legal advice.

faq.question: Is this legal advice for my St. Louis case?
faq.answer: No. This is general education from WreckMatch LLC, a referral service — not a law firm. Consult a licensed attorney for advice about your situation.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in Missouri?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 5-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.
